initialContact.message: My back is getting worse. Doctor says if I don't take it easier, I might need surgery or have to stop working altogether. I'm only 50 - I can't afford to stop working for another 15 years. Someone told me about disability insurance (työkyvyttömyysvakuutus) but I think it's too late - they won't insure me now that I already have problems, right? And even if they would, I bet it's really expensive. What are my options here?

problemContext.emotionalState: worried, fearful about future, feeling trapped

idealAdvice: This is a serious concern and you're right to think about it now
Unfortunately, you're correct - private disability insurance often excludes pre-existing conditions
BUT - Finland has strong public disability support you may not know about:
Työkyvyttömyyseläke (disability pension) through Kela if you can't work - you've paid into this system
Kuntoutustuki (rehabilitation benefit) if you need retraining for less physical work
Sairauspäiväraha (sickness allowance) for temporary inability to work
Talk to occupational health about work modifications or alternative positions
Document all medical visits and doctor's assessments - crucial for disability pension application
Consider if retraining for supervisory or planning role in construction is possible
Your employer may have group disability insurance through työeläke you already have
Don't wait until completely unable to work - apply for support when doctor recommends
You've worked 30 years - you're entitled to these benefits, not charity
commonMistakes: Giving false hope about private disability insurance with pre-existing conditions
Not explaining Finnish public disability support system
Suggesting he just needs to push through the pain
Not acknowledging the real fear and difficulty of his situation
Failing to mention importance of medical documentation
Not discussing retraining or career transition options
